title: Local Knowledge Index Registration (search-runtime, M08)
description: D-079: the public Loopback contract that turns an *installed* Knowledge asset into an *activated* one. Before this contract existed, `services/search-runtime` could only search index directories it found under its own `INDEX_BASE` tree (written locally by indexing-runtime, M07) — so a Knowledge that arrived through the Offline Bundle path and was installed by Desktop (M04) into the per-user install root was on disk, listed as "설치됨", and yet unsearchable, with nothing in the product saying so. M04 must NOT fix that by writing into M08's INDEX_BASE tree or importing M08 internals (CLAUDE.md 구현 원칙 2); it registers the installed directory through these endpoints instead, and search-runtime decides — from its own deployment policy — whether that directory may be searched at all. Registration is deliberately refusable and every refusal is explicit: an index this service will not search must never look like an index that simply found no results. Scope note: this contract covers Knowledge only. Activating an installed MCP Tool (agent-runtime/Office Profile server+tool registry) is the other half of D-079 and is NOT covered here.

LocalIndexSource.description: Provenance of the index directory being registered. A closed enum, not free text: search-runtime applies stricter artifact rules to distributed content than to locally-built content (see D-054 — a `bm25.pkl` that travelled inside a Bundle is executable content this service will not unpickle), so the caller has to name the channel it came from rather than describe it.

knowledge_id.description: The AssetVersion id this index was built for — the same id `knowledge-search.schema.json`'s SearchRequest.knowledge_id carries, NOT the parent Asset id (D-060). Verified against the index's own `index-meta.json` at registration time; a mismatch is refused rather than trusted.

index_path.description: Absolute, symlink-resolved directory containing this Knowledge's `index-meta.json`, `bm25.json` and `chroma/`. Echoed back so an operator/diagnostic screen can show exactly which directory was activated.

label.description: Optional human-readable Knowledge name for operator display (e.g. "재택근무 정책 Knowledge v1.0.0"). Display only — never used to resolve a path.

RegisterLocalIndexRequest.description: POST /search/v1/local-indexes. Idempotent per `knowledge_id`: re-registering the same id replaces the entry (a Desktop re-install of the same version must not need a delete first). Every field is caller-asserted and none of them is trusted on its own — see the refusal list on RegisterLocalIndexResponse.

RegisterLocalIndexResponse.description: 200 only when the directory was accepted AND is searchable now. Refusals use the common Error Envelope (07-data-api-contracts.md §10.2) with `details.reason` naming exactly one cause, and `error.message` carrying a user-facing Korean sentence the caller can display verbatim. The complete reason list — a caller may switch on these, and the service raises no others: `local_indexes_disabled` (this deployment configured no allowed root — 403 PERMISSION_DENIED), `path_outside_allowed_roots` (403 PERMISSION_DENIED, checked after symlink resolution so a link pointing out of the root cannot smuggle a path past it), `path_not_absolute`, `path_not_a_directory`, `knowledge_id_invalid` (not an AssetVersion UUID — refused before the value can reach the path layer), `index_meta_missing`, `index_meta_unreadable`, `index_meta_knowledge_id_mismatch` (the directory's own metadata disagrees with the claimed id — the D-060 class of bug, refused instead of believed), `bm25_missing`, `bm25_legacy_pickle_only` (D-054: only an unmigrated executable `bm25.pkl` is present; run convert-bm25-format), `chroma_missing`, `central_index_exists` (a same-id index already exists under this service's own INDEX_BASE — refused so a registered directory can never silently shadow locally-built content), `source_not_allowed`, `label_too_long` — all 400 VALIDATION_ERROR unless noted.

local_indexes_enabled.description: False when this deployment configured no allowed root, i.e. registration would be refused. Exposed so a caller can distinguish "nothing activated yet" from "activation is not available on this deployment" without having to attempt a registration and read the error.

ListLocalIndexesResponse.description: GET /search/v1/local-indexes. Returns only entries that still pass re-validation at read time (the directory can be deleted or moved by the user after registration) — a stale entry is reported as `active: false` by the caller-side activation state, never silently listed as if it worked.

removed.description: False when no entry existed for this id. Deliberately a 200 with an explicit `false` rather than a 404: deactivation on uninstall must be safe to call unconditionally, but the caller still gets to see that nothing was actually deregistered.

DeleteLocalIndexResponse.description: DELETE /search/v1/local-indexes/{knowledge_id}. Removes the registration only — this service never deletes the index files themselves, which belong to whoever installed them (M04).
